description: A pool of nodes for services on the Kubernetes platform. Every replica becomes a pod scheduled by its CPU and memory requests; pods wait as Pending when nodes are full until the cluster autoscaler adds a node, then pull their image and start.
modeled: Nodes with allocatable CPU and memory; pods bound by their requests to the least allocated node that fits
Pending pods when no node has room; scheduled as soon as room appears
Cluster autoscaler: scan interval, node provisioning delay, max/min nodes, removal of empty nodes
Image pull on the first pod of a service per node, then the service's start-up time
Services join automatically (the only cluster) or by name; each replica is a pod
notModeled: CPU contention between pods beyond their requests (noisy neighbours), limits and throttling
Pod priority and preemption, affinity, taints, topology spread
Node failures, drains and rolling deployments

presets.description: Three 4 vCPU / 16 GiB nodes with the cluster autoscaler (up to 10 nodes, 2 minutes per node). Node sizes, provisioning times and prices are illustrative.
presets.name: Kubernetes cluster

presets.description: Managed control plane with a node group of 4 vCPU / 16 GiB instances, about 2.5 minutes per new node. Node sizes, provisioning times and prices are illustrative.
presets.name: EKS-style managed cluster

presets.description: Managed cluster with 4 vCPU / 16 GiB nodes and node auto-provisioning, about 1.5 minutes per new node. Node sizes, provisioning times and prices are illustrative.
presets.name: GKE-style managed cluster

presets.description: Managed cluster with 4 vCPU / 16 GiB nodes, about 3 minutes per new node. Node sizes, provisioning times and prices are illustrative.
presets.name: AKS-style managed cluster

presets.description: Lightweight Kubernetes on two small nodes and no cluster autoscaler: what fits is what you get. Node sizes, provisioning times and prices are illustrative.
presets.name: k3s (small / edge)

aks.detail: Each pod reserves the CPU and memory it requests on one node; the scheduler only binds it to a node with that much unreserved, and prefers the least allocated node.
aks.title: Pods are scheduled by their requests

aks.detail: When no node has room for a pod's requests it stays Pending: the replica the autoscaler asked for does not exist yet and takes no traffic.
aks.title: Pending pods

aks.detail: Every 10 s the cluster autoscaler looks for Pending pods and adds nodes for them; a new node takes minutes to boot and join. Nodes left empty for 10 minutes are removed.
aks.title: Cluster autoscaler

aks.detail: The first pod of a service on a node pulls its container image before starting; later pods on that node reuse the cached image.
aks.title: Image pulls on new nodes

aks.detail: The HPA re-evaluates every 15 s by default and asks for more pods; they still have to be scheduled, pulled and started before they help.
aks.title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
